high.title: DI Rates Fall Sharply as Below-Expected IPCA Reinforces Selic Cut Expectations for August
high.summary: Brazil's interest rate futures curve closed sharply lower on Friday (July 10), with declines of approximately 20 basis points across multiple maturities, following an inflation print that came in below market consensus. The move significantly reinforced market expectations for a Selic rate cut at the August COPOM meeting. The short-end January 2027 DI rate fell 9bps to 13.900% (from 13.990%), while the medium-term January 2029 DI rate dropped more aggressively to 13.980% from 14.205% — a decline of approximately 22.5bps — signaling a meaningful repricing of the easing cycle. For fixed income investors, this presents an important signal: the market is now more confidently pricing in rate cuts, which should support Brazilian government bond prices across the curve. Bond investors should watch whether this repricing holds into the following week and monitor any COPOM member communications that could either confirm or temper easing expectations. The softer inflation data and resulting rate expectations also carry positive spillover effects for BRL and equity valuations.

high.title: Ibovespa Surges 3%, Closing at 177,000 Points on Selic Cut Hopes; Dollar Falls to R$5.10
high.summary: The Ibovespa surged nearly 3% on Friday (July 10), jumping from 172,000 to close at 177,866 points — its intraday high — driven by benign inflation data that amplified expectations for a Selic rate cut at the next COPOM meeting. The index gained 2.97% on the day and 2.18% for the week, reflecting a broad-based risk-on rally across Brazilian equities. Simultaneously, the USD/BRL spot rate fell 0.28% to R$5.1084, touching an intraday low of R$5.0990 (-0.46%), marking the third consecutive session of dollar weakness against the Real. On a weekly basis, the dollar retreated 1.17% against BRL. The dual rally in equities and currency reflects a coherent macro narrative: lower-than-expected inflation is compressing rate expectations, boosting risk appetite and attracting flows into Brazilian assets. For equity traders, the 177,000 level is a key milestone to watch for follow-through momentum. For FX traders, the R$5.10 handle is now a technically significant support/resistance zone, and a sustained break below R$5.10 would represent a meaningful BRL strengthening signal. Investors should monitor U.S. Treasury yield dynamics, which are also providing a tailwind for BRL via external dollar weakness.

high.title: Dollar Falls to R$5.10 on Increased Bets for Selic Cut Following IPCA Surprise
high.summary: The USD/BRL spot rate extended its losing streak to three consecutive sessions, closing at R$5.1084 on Friday (July 10), down 0.28% on the day, with an intraday low of R$5.0990. The BRL's appreciation was driven by a combination of domestic factors — primarily the below-consensus IPCA reading that boosted Selic cut expectations — and a broader softening of the U.S. dollar globally, supported by easing U.S. Treasury yields. This confluence of domestic monetary policy repricing and external USD weakness created a particularly supportive environment for the Real. For FX traders, the key near-term question is whether BRL can sustain a move through the R$5.10 level and whether the IPCA-driven narrative will be reinforced by additional data or COPOM guidance in the coming week. The R$5.0990 intraday low now serves as an immediate target for bulls, while any reversal in U.S. yields or a hawkish surprise from BCB communication could quickly challenge the current momentum.

high.title: CSN Mineração (CMIN3) Surges 21% and MRV (MRVE3) Posts Worst Weekly Balance on Ibovespa; Weekly Highlights
high.summary:
The Ibovespa extended its winning streak to three consecutive weeks, closing the latest session at 177,866.37 points with a weekly gain of 2.18%. The rally was driven by two key catalysts: optimism surrounding resumed US-Iran peace negotiations in the Middle East, which eased geopolitical risk sentiment, and growing market expectations that Banco Central do Brasil (BCB) will continue its monetary easing cycle. On the FX front, the Brazilian Real strengthened materially against the dollar, with the USD/BRL spot rate closing at R$5.1084 — a weekly depreciation of 1.17% for the dollar. This BRL appreciation reflects improving risk appetite and dovish BCB expectations feeding into carry trade dynamics. For bond investors, continued bets on monetary easing support duration positioning in Brazilian government bonds. Traders should monitor any BCB communications or COPOM signals that could confirm or challenge the easing narrative, as well as geopolitical developments in the Middle East that could shift global risk sentiment and impact capital flows into Brazilian assets.

medium.title: Musical Chairs: BofA Assesses Which Stocks May Enter and Exit Ibovespa in First Preliminary Review
medium.summary:
Bank of America has released a preliminary assessment of potential changes to the Ibovespa composition ahead of the first preview of the new portfolio, due to be published on August 3. BofA estimates that Tenda (TEND3) and Itaú Unibanco ordinary shares (ITUB3) could be added to the index, while PetroReconcavo (RECV3) is flagged as a potential exclusion. The potential inclusion of Itaú's ordinary shares (ITUB3) is of particular relevance to institutional investors, as Itaú is one of Brazil's largest banks and its addition could influence passive fund flows into the stock. BofA cautioned that these are preliminary estimates and subject to revision. Index rebalancing events can generate short-term trading opportunities and passive inflow effects worth monitoring.
